newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French CIC bank reports 1996 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French CIC bank reports 1996 profit rise.

text.p: French regional banking group CIC, a subsidiary of state-owned Groupe GAN, reported on Monday that net attributable profit rose 36 percent last year to 847 million francs ($148.9 million).
The company said it expected to show further profit growth this year and enter the private sector.
"This year should register a new and marked progression in results and also mark the CIC Group's entry into the private sector," the group said in a results statement.
CIC's net banking income rose to 17.13 billion francs from 16.56 billion. Operating costs climbed to 13.11 billion francs from 12.90 billion.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis scrapped his first attempt to sell CIC when he cancelled a privatisation tender last November after getting just one eligible offer -- from Banque Nationale Paris -- for the group, which comprises 13 regional banks and has strong local links with small businesses.

But he has vowed to sell off the bank, which is regarded as the jewel in GAN's crown, as well as to pump 20 billion francs into GAN itself to shore up a balance sheet ruined mainly by losses in a collapsed property market.
Both will be privatised this year, Arthuis says.

CIC chairman Philippe Pontet, brought in last year after Arthuis fired the heads of both GAN and CIC for criticising the government's privatisation plans, said the banking group was seeking a quality majority shareholder.
He said he opposed dismantling the bank and was also against a buyout by its own regional banks, an idea floated in the French press.

"There is no question of selling CIC in bits, by sectors," Pontet told a news conference. "We are seeking a majority, quality shareholder as our main shareholder, with GAN the second biggest shareholder." ($ = 5.689 French Francs)
